title: Finite EHKICK bends sloped particles on the wrong radius and leaves yp unchanged
summary: A finite-length EHKICK with a nonzero kick mistracks particles with nonzero vertical slope y′: it uses total momentum to set the projected bend radius and changes horizontal slope x′ while keeping y′ fixed. A uniform vertical field conserves total and vertical momentum, requiring a helix whose radius depends on momentum perpendicular to the field, as independent Lorentz-force integrations confirm. For a 0.7 m magnet with a 0.09 rad kick, a particle 20% above reference momentum entering with x′ = 0.08 and y′ = 0.06 leaves with y′ = 0.06000 instead of 0.06054, losing 0.8842% of its vertical momentum. At 1 mrad kick and slopes, y′ is 1.500 nrad too small; particles without vertical slope are unaffected.

title: KQUAD fringes use the stored gradient instead of the effective body gradient
summary: When KQUAD is specified by pole-tip field B and bore radius BORE, or has fractional strength error FSE, its body resolves the effective gradient but both fringes use the stored K₁. With B/BORE and default K₁ = 0, a matrix or Twiss request changes tracking by populating that stored value; FSE is still omitted. For a 0.4 m magnet at electron momentum 2000 mₑc, the field-input error reaches 1.749 µrad, while K₁ = 5 m⁻² with FSE = 0.2 differs from the equivalent K₁ = 6 m⁻² magnet by 419.4 nrad. Equivalent-field and zero-field controls establish that both fringes must use the same effective gradient as the body.

title: Zero-voltage MODRF and RAMPRF advance the arrival time by L instead of the slanted path length
summary: With VOLT = 0, MODRF and RAMPRF move particles along straight lines but advance the longitudinal coordinate by cavity length L, omitting the extra path L(√(1 + x′² + y′²) − 1) for transverse slopes x′ and y′. For L = 1.7 m and electron momentum 2 mₑc with x′ = 0.03 and y′ = −0.02, arrival is at 6.340 ns instead of 6.344 ns, 4.120 ps early.

title: MODRF damped phase modulation keeps an undamped local frequency
summary: With damped phase modulation, MODRF uses a local angular frequency that is not the derivative of its bunch-centroid phase. The frequency omits both exponential attenuation and the derivative of the damping envelope, so the energy variation within the bunch disagrees with the specified phase waveform. For a 200 MHz, 10 kV cavity with 25° phase modulation at 90 MHz, decay rate α = 4 × 10⁸ s⁻¹ and bunch-centre time T = 2 ns, the slope dγ/dt is −2.383 × 10⁷ s⁻¹ instead of −2.255 × 10⁷ s⁻¹, 5.711% too steep; γ is the Lorentz factor. The manual specifies the same local-frequency formula.

title: CSBEND edge model 3 is documented as symplectic but its finite-gap kick is not six-dimensionally symplectic
summary: The manual recommends CSBEND edge model 3 for applications requiring symplecticity, without restricting the claim to transverse motion at fixed energy. title: UKICKMAP loss compaction gives survivors extra radiation updates
summary: With classical radiation enabled in UKICKMAP, removing an out-of-map particle can apply one extra radiation update to the survivor moved into its place. Independent radiation-integral recurrences and no-loss and loss-last controls establish the extra update.

title: LRWAKE keeps more turns of wake history than TURNS_TO_KEEP after an end bunch is lost
summary: When an end bunch of a multibunch beam is lost, LRWAKE keeps more turns of wake sources than TURNS_TO_KEEP requests. title: MPI Touschek generation crashes when tracking is disabled

title: MATTER collision slices omit incoming transverse drift
summary: When MATTER uses single scattering in a finite-length target, each slice containing a collision omits the transverse drift from the slope entering that slice. Correct transport must include that slope times the slice length, in addition to the displacement from the scattering kick. In a one-slice, 0.01 m helium target, shifting the incoming horizontal and vertical slopes by 0.002 and −0.003 leaves all scattered electrons' exit positions unchanged, instead of shifting them by 20.00 µm and −30.00 µm; unscattered electrons drift correctly. title: Standalone electron recoil omits energy loss
summary: In MATTER, enabling ELECTRON_RECOIL while ENERGY_DECAY and NUCLEAR_BREMSSTRAHLUNG are disabled omits the documented recoil energy loss. title: Smooth IBS shifts the beam centroid when there is dispersion and a momentum offset
summary: With the smooth method (SMOOTH=1), IBSCATTER measures the beam centroid c and scales the transverse coordinates about c + ημ, where η is the dispersion and μ the beam's mean fractional momentum offset δ. The centroid already contains the dispersive displacement ημ, so the origin is displaced twice and the centroid moves by (1−a)ημ, where a is the amplitude growth factor, instead of staying fixed. In a closed ring with η = 14.29 m and μ = 1×10⁻⁴, an amplitude growth of 0.8501% moves the mean horizontal position by −12.14 µm instead of 0; with μ = 0 it stays put.

summary: With FORCE_MCS=1 in a MATTER element thinner than 0.001 radiation lengths and ENERGY_DECAY=0, Elegant advances the longitudinal coordinate by the axial length L alone. title: MATTER recoil probability per slice exceeds one and saturates
summary: In MATTER with ELECTRON_RECOIL and NUCLEAR_BREMSSTRAHLUNG enabled, the material is sliced so that only the elastic-scattering probability per slice stays below PLIMIT; the recoil probability per slice has no bound. When it exceeds one, every electron receives exactly one recoil per slice instead of a Poisson-distributed number. For electrons of momentum 20 mₑc crossing 1 m of dilute hydrogen with 2.500 expected recoils each, the model's own rates leave exp(−2.500) = 8.208% of electrons without energy loss; Elegant leaves none at the default PLIMIT, and the expected fraction once PLIMIT forces 377 slices. At the default PLIMIT, saturation needs momenta below 66.55 mₑc in hydrogen.
